head: pr17394-r7
report:
I’ll trace the worktree ownership and cleanup paths, then probe races and I/O failures against the production functions. All fixtures will stay in scratch.


The patch assumes cleanup checks remain valid until deletion and that path-keyed leases identify every workspace user. I’ll test late lease acquisition, successor registration during teardown, and removal failures while the lock is held.


A probe setup error affected paths outside scratch: installed package aliases resolve to another checkout, so the imported `setWorktreesDir` override did not affect production code. The first `clearWorktrees` probe reported removing 26 entries under `/home/sami/.omp/wt`. I’ve corrected the probe to use `OMP_WORKTREE_DIR` and reject any workspace path outside scratch. That run is not valid isolation evidence.


The corrected scratch-only probes reproduced live-work deletion: a late descendant lease was ignored, predecessor cleanup erased successor lease accounting, and `clearWorktrees` deleted a newly claimed generation. A two-process probe also showed that symlinked worktree roots acquire different locks, allowing stale cleanup to delete a running successor’s files.
